concerns.concern: Decorrelation is not shown to come from domain rearrangement. No traces of total Bragg intensity, peak centre-of-mass, peak width or sample position versus time are given, so instrumental, thermal and normalisation artefacts are not excluded.
concerns.quote: The paper gives no traces of total Bragg intensity, peak centre-of-mass (in 2θ and ω), peak width, or sample position versus time.

concerns.concern: Joule heating at 4 mA (about 8 mW) could shift the lattice parameter, move intensity between the M1 and R peaks, or displace the sample. Any of these would erase the speckle without changing domain topology.
concerns.quote: Any of these shifts the speckle pattern and produces "immediate erasure" (Fig. 3b) without any change in domain topology.

concerns.concern: The ~1000 s delayed decorrelation under sub-threshold current has the timescale expected for slow thermal drift of the probe station after a small heat load is switched on.
concerns.quote: The ~1000 s delayed decorrelation at 0.26 mA (Fig. 3a) has the timescale expected for slow thermal drift of a probe station

concerns.concern: The two-time correlation normalisation in Eq. 1 is non-standard, so any change in mean intensity (e.g. a phase-fraction change) shows up as a change in correlation. It should be recomputed with the standard pixel-ensemble normalisation over a defined ROI.
concerns.quote: With this form, any change of mean intensity, for example from a phase-fraction change, appears as a change in "correlation".

concerns.concern: The measured relaxation times are at or beyond the stated experimental stability limit. The 4 mA On-state τ exceeds the room-temperature limit, and the 0.26 mA τ is within about a factor of two of it.
concerns.quote: These dynamics are therefore at or below the demonstrated noise floor.

concerns.concern: Key controls are missing: drift correction or speckle registration with before/after maps, external heating to the estimated temperature without current, and a non-switching reference region or device under the same heat load.
concerns.quote: Run a control in which the sample is heated externally by the temperature rise estimated for each current, with no current applied.

concerns.concern: The fitted τ values far exceed the observation window, and g₂ never approaches baseline. β and τ are therefore almost fully degenerate, and the contrast A is not independently known, so the β-based 'jamming transition' is weakly constrained.
concerns.quote: For t ≪ τ, |F|² ≈ 1 − 2(t/τ)^β, so β and τ are almost fully degenerate.

concerns.concern: Forcing a single τ for all ageing times while β is free pushes any ageing-induced change in τ, or drift-induced curvature, into an apparent rise in β.
concerns.quote: The Methods impose one τ for all t_age, with β free. Any ageing-induced change in τ is then forced into β.

concerns.concern: The statistics behind the β transition are weak. Error bars are large, several points have β<1, and the 4 mA curve never clearly reaches 1.5. Free fits with covariance, model comparison and A fixed from static speckle are requested.
concerns.quote: Error bars are large, several points have β<1 (stretched exponentials), and the 4 mA curve never clearly reaches 1.5.

concerns.concern: The stochastic-to-deterministic switching claim rests only on XPCS correlation. No per-cycle electrical statistics (R_On, R_Off, threshold, switching delay, variance) are reported for the cycling run.
concerns.quote: "Deterministic switching" is defined only through XPCS correlation, so the title and abstract claims about switching stochasticity are not tested electrically.

concerns.concern: There is no check that the device returns to the Off state each cycle. Rising cycle-to-cycle correlation could simply mean the device stops switching off and approaches the steady 4 mA state; Off-phase frames are requested.
concerns.quote: rising cycle-to-cycle correlation simply means the device stops switching off.

concerns.concern: The rise time of the cycle-to-cycle correlation (~1000 cycles ≈ 3000 s) is comparable to thermal equilibration times, so it may be a thermal effect.
concerns.quote: The rise time (~1000 cycles ≈ 3000 s) is also comparable to the thermal equilibration times discussed in concern 1.

concerns.concern: Only adjacent-cycle correlations are shown. Long-lag G(n,m) is needed, since determinism implies late cycles correlate with each other at all lags.
concerns.quote: Show G(n,m) for long lags |n−m|, not only adjacent cycles.

concerns.concern: The normalisation of ΔG (to what minimum and maximum) is not defined.
concerns.quote: Define how ΔG is normalised (to what minimum and maximum).

concerns.concern: Cycling controls are missing: the same average power delivered as DC, and sub-threshold pulsing.
concerns.quote: Run controls with the same average power delivered as DC, and with sub-threshold pulsing.

concerns.concern: The train-and-reset (erasure of short-term memory) claim is not demonstrated. The only sub-threshold experiment acts on the pristine state, and no train, erase, retest sequence is shown. The authors should perform it or soften the claim.
concerns.quote: The erasure-and-reset functionality, which is the neuromorphic selling point, is therefore an extrapolation.

concerns.concern: The X-ray footprint is several times larger than the 5×5 µm channel. Much of the signal may come from VO₂ under the electrodes or outside the gap rather than the filament; the footprint, the in-channel fraction, a diffraction map and the ROIs should be given.
concerns.quote: Much of the diffracted intensity therefore comes from VO₂ under the electrodes and outside the gap, which does not carry current.

concerns.concern: Scattering from Au(111) electrodes, which is itself sensitive to Joule heating, may fall within the detector range and should be explicitly excluded.
concerns.quote: Contamination by electrode scattering, which is itself sensitive to Joule heating, should be explicitly excluded.

concerns.concern: Changes are attributed to metallic R versus insulating M1 domains, but whole images appear to be correlated. Separate correlation analyses on each side of the split peak are needed.
concerns.quote: The text attributes changes to metallic 011_R versus insulating 200_M1 domains, but whole images appear to be correlated.

concerns.concern: X-ray beam effects (oxygen vacancies, local heating, photo-carriers) could drive the slow dynamics and the 'training'. A dose-dependence control and R(t) with the beam on versus off are needed.
concerns.quote: beam-induced changes in VO₂ are plausible: oxygen-vacancy creation, local heating, photo-carriers. These could drive the slow dynamics and the "training".

concerns.concern: The current-driven dynamics are attributed to Joule heating, yet the 4 mA τ is longer than the zero-current τ even at 298 K. This is inconsistent; the local temperature rise should be estimated and compared with τ.
concerns.quote: Either the On state is stabilised by a non-thermal mechanism, or τ is unresolved (concern 1).

concerns.concern: The Arrhenius analysis uses only two temperatures, which cannot test activated behaviour, and the ±800 K uncertainty is unexplained. At least 4–5 temperatures in the stationary regime are requested.
concerns.quote: A 2-point "Arrhenius law" cannot test activated behaviour, and the ±800 K uncertainty is not explained.

concerns.concern: Neither Arrhenius point is a clean measurement. The 298 K point is only a stability bound, and the 340 K data are non-stationary, so a t_age-independent fit is inappropriate.
concerns.quote: The 340 K data are acknowledged to be non-stationary (contrast drops along the diagonal, Fig. 2b) at the transition, where a t_age-independent fit is inappropriate.

concerns.concern: Comparing the activation energy with the melting temperature has no physical basis and should be removed or justified.
concerns.quote: equates an activation barrier with k_B·T_m. That comparison is not physically meaningful and should be removed or properly justified.

concerns.concern: The sub-threshold case shows the same β transition without any filament. This contradicts the idea that switching or filament formation drives jamming and suggests a generic, possibly instrumental or thermal-drift, origin.
concerns.quote: The 0.26/0.27 mA case shows the same β transition without any filament.

concerns.concern: The jamming times for different currents are statistically indistinguishable, so the claimed trend (larger current, slower transition) is not supported.
concerns.quote: t_jam = 1100±600, 1200±500 and 4000±3000 s are statistically indistinguishable

concerns.concern: Jamming and compressed-exponential physics are invoked on β alone. Independent signatures are needed: q-dependence of τ, growing τ(t_age), broadening along the two-time diagonal, and dynamic heterogeneity.
concerns.quote: Before invoking jamming in "hard matter", one would expect evidence beyond β

concerns.concern: The terminology is loose: β=1 does not by itself mean liquid-like dynamics, equilibrium glasses show stretched rather than compressed exponentials, and 'glassy' and 'jammed' are used interchangeably.
concerns.quote: β=1 does not by itself indicate "liquid-like" dynamics.

concerns.concern: Two-time maps and g₂ curves at 1.7 mA are not shown, and it is not stated whether this current is above or below the switching thresholds.
concerns.quote: Two-time maps and g₂ curves for 1.7 mA are not shown.

concerns.concern: Each protocol appears to have been run once on one device, and the order of measurements and any resets between them are not given, although the paper claims history matters. Repeated runs on multiple devices are needed.
concerns.quote: Each protocol appears to have been run once on one (irradiated) device; the pristine device is relegated to the SI.

concerns.concern: Several statements exceed what XPCS can show: domain reconfiguration localised 'around the conductive filament', and initial domain distribution influencing filament formation.
concerns.quote: XPCS gives no spatial localisation.

concerns.concern: The text says domain speeds are derived from the correlation decay in the Methods, but no such derivation exists and no speeds are reported.
concerns.quote: the Methods contain no such derivation, and no speeds are reported.

concerns.concern: The irradiation geometry is inconsistent: the main text says only a central 5×5 µm region was irradiated, while the Methods say devices were globally irradiated.
concerns.quote: The main text says a "central 5×5 µm region" was irradiated and the other device is pristine; the Methods say devices were "globally irradiated".

concerns.concern: The authors should discuss how irradiation, which ref. 7 reports enhances stochasticity, affects the stochastic-to-deterministic crossover.
concerns.quote: Please discuss how irradiation affects the stochastic-to-deterministic crossover.

concerns.concern: The speckle contrast achieved is not stated. Contrast is likely ~2% given the coherence length versus footprint, and its effect on per-frame signal-to-noise in the cycling experiment should be discussed.
concerns.quote: State the speckle contrast (β_coh/A) achieved.

concerns.concern: The domain-size estimate of 20 nm should be discussed against the 45 nm film thickness and strain broadening, with the Q_FWHM direction and instrumental resolution specified.
concerns.quote: R_d = 2π/Q_FWHM = 20 nm should be discussed against the 45 nm film thickness and strain broadening

concerns.concern: Relaxation times disagree between text and figures: room temperature is 8000±3000 s in the text but 81 000±3000 s in Fig. 2c, and 4 mA is 150 000 s in the text but 160 000 s in Fig. 3h.
concerns.quote: The text gives "8000±3000 s" while Fig. 2c gives τ = 81 000 ± 3000 s.

concerns.concern: Cycle timing is inconsistent: 200 cycles corresponds to ~600 s on the axis, and the text says 3 s on and off while the axis implies a ~2.8 s period. The cycle period and duty cycle should be clarified.
concerns.quote: Please clarify the cycle period and duty cycle: the text says "on and off for 3 s", while the axis implies a ~2.8 s period.

concerns.concern: The text says correlation 'stabilizes for ≈1000 cycles', whereas the figure shows a plateau reached after ~1000 cycles.
concerns.quote: the figure and caption indicate a plateau reached after ~1000 cycles.

concerns.concern: Fig. 5b should give numerical values of I₁, I₂, I_On and I_Off, and the On-state resistance at 4 mA.
concerns.quote: Give numerical values of I₁, I₂, I_On and I_Off, and the On-state resistance at 4 mA.

concerns.concern: The meaning of error bars in Figs. 2–4 (fit standard error versus spread) is not stated.
concerns.quote: The meaning of error bars in Figs. 2–4 (fit standard error versus spread) should be stated.

concerns.concern: The sub-threshold current is given inconsistently as 0.26 mA in Fig. 3 and 0.27 mA in the Fig. 4 text.
concerns.quote: The sub-threshold current is 0.26 mA in Fig. 3 and 0.27 mA in the Fig. 4 text.

concerns.concern: The text refers to an inset for ΔG(n,n+1), but the data are in the main panel of Fig. 3i.
concerns.quote: The text refers to "the inset (orange data)" for ΔG(n,n+1), but this is the main panel, Fig. 3i.

concerns.concern: The Bragg angle is misstated: '~50°' is the scattering angle 2θ, so θ ≈ 25°.
concerns.quote: "Bragg angle ∼50°" should read 2θ ≈ 50° (θ ≈ 25°).

concerns.concern: Diffraction intensity is incorrectly described as the absolute value of the Fourier transform rather than its squared modulus.
concerns.quote: Diffraction intensity is the squared modulus of the Fourier transform, not "the absolute value".

concerns.concern: Eq. 3 is mislabelled as a single exponential decay when it is a KWW stretched/compressed exponential.
concerns.quote: It is a KWW stretched/compressed exponential, not a "single exponential decay".

concerns.concern: The two-time colour maps are wrongly called 'three-dimensional plots'.
concerns.quote: "Three-dimensional plots" should read two-time colour maps.

concerns.concern: The Fig. 1 caption refers to top/center/bottom of panel c, but the figure has separate panels c, d and e.
concerns.quote: It describes the "top/center/bottom" of panel c, but the figure has separate panels c, d, e.

concerns.concern: Panel 'C' in Fig. 3 should be lower-case.
concerns.quote: Panel "C" should be lower-case.
